# rlsbl scaffold

Render the release infrastructure of the member whose directory is the working directory, from rlsbl's templates and .strictmetadata/releasables/releasables.toml, and keep it current. Each target the member has (declared, or detected from its manifests) gets its CI workflow (ci.yml, or ci-<target>.yml beside another target's), a Go module its VERSION and, for a go binary pipeline, .goreleaser.yml and version.go, an npm package its .npmignore (written once, then the project's), and an npm go-binary package its bin/index.js launcher. A releasable publishing from CI gets .github/workflows/publish.yml: the wait-for-ci job, then one job per pipeline publishing from CI, rendered without build attestations, Go proxy requests, or repository URLs where the lifecycle-and-license record or GitHub's visibility forbids them. Every member gets the .gitignore lines it lacks, the experiments/ and screenshots/ scratch directories, stub go.mod files keeping private directories out of a Go module (.strictmetadata/go.mod at the root), a LICENSE written once from the record's license in effect when rlsbl carries its text, and, while rlsbl:test-sandbox is on, the sandboxed test runner. pyproject.toml gains pytest's norecursedirs, its ignores of nested members, and hatchling's sdist exclusions. The pre-push and post-rewrite git hooks are installed where git runs them. An existing file is merged three ways against its merge base under .strictmetadata/.scaffold-bases/ (a missing base is rebuilt from the file's last `rlsbl scaffold` commit); a conflict is written with git's markers, left uncommitted, and fails the command. A file scaffold managed and no longer renders is removed through saferm while unmodified. Everything is planned and every refusal made before anything is written; the managed files and their hashes are recorded in .strictmetadata/.scaffold-state/scaffold-state.toml. While rlsbl:ecosystem-tagging is on, the npm and PyPI manifests gain the rlsbl keyword and the repository the rlsbl topic. A workspace's root member is not scaffolded: `rlsbl monorepo sync --auto-commit` generates its workflows. Scaffolding any other member of a workspace ends by regenerating the workspace's CI router and publish router from the members' workflows, as monorepo sync does, committed with the same choice as the scaffold; under --dry-run that step is named, not previewed.

**Effect:** mutating

## Flags

| Name | Short | Type | Presence | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--target` |  | str | optional |  | A target the member must have: one it neither declares nor has detected is added to its declared targets (with the targets it has) in .strictmetadata/releasables/releasables.toml Values: `go` (a Go module), `npm` (an npm package), `pypi` (a Python package). |
| `--publish-mode` |  | str | optional |  | The publish mode to declare for the member's releasable in .strictmetadata/releasables/releasables.toml Values: `ci` (publish through the scaffolded CI publish workflow), `none` (publish nothing to any registry). |
| `--auto-commit`, `--no-auto-commit` |  | bool | optional |  | Commit what the run wrote, with the Autogenerated trailer (committed when neither --auto-commit nor --no-auto-commit is passed) |
| `--skip-shared`, `--no-skip-shared` |  | bool | optional |  | Leave the files every member gets (.gitignore, scratch directories, stub go.mod files, LICENSE, the test runner) as they are (rendered when neither --skip-shared nor --no-skip-shared is passed) |
